restaurant-concept.png.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Create a polished low-poly sushi restaurant game concept from these references using TWO DIFFERENT ART PROJECTIONS in one coherent scene.

IMAGE ROLES AND PRIORITY:
Image 1 is the authoritative ENVIRONMENT GEOMETRY AND LAYOUT GUIDE. Preserve its true square floor cells, parallel edges, square top faces, rectangular front faces, object positions, scale, and L conveyor footprint while turning its simple flat colors into beautiful finished low-poly game art. Its cyan crosses indicate standing feet roots; orange dots indicate seated hip/seat contact points. These markers are planning aids to replace with characters, never show them in the final.
Image 2 is the user's UNDERWATER ENVIRONMENT PROJECTION REFERENCE. Match the way its square tiled floor and raised crates, columns, rock walls and platforms show clear tops and fronts at uniform scale along the screen. Transfer that environmental view to the restaurant. It is a projection/rendering reference, not the restaurant subject or palette.
Image 3 is the RESTAURANT THEME, CHARACTER AND UI REFERENCE. Keep its warm cream floor, red/charcoal sushi belt, wood, lanterns, red entrance curtain, expansion-edge rocks and plants, cheerful blocky characters, coin counter and three UI buttons. Copy its character proportions and style; its receding floor/perspective is superseded by images 1 and 2.

ENVIRONMENT PROJECTION:
Use square top/front oblique projection for ALL floor, conveyor, stools, serving tables, prep stands, entrance, pots, crates and terrain. The FLOOR IS A FLAT, SCREEN-ALIGNED GRID OF TRUE SQUARES of constant pitch: in image 1 each cell is 112 pixels wide and 112 pixels tall on a 1024x1536 canvas, with seams at x=64+112*n, y=272+112*n. Preserve this identical horizontal AND vertical spacing over the whole canvas, behind and around objects. All ground north-south edges are exactly screen-vertical; all east-west edges exactly screen-horizontal. No narrowing toward the doorway, no foreshortening of distant rows, no perspective convergence, no diamond grid.
For grid-aligned objects, TOP planes are true-shape, with a one-cell top being a visible 112x112 square. A front plane also keeps its own width/height ratio. Raising an object shifts its top straight upward over the row behind, exposing its front below it; height does not shrink its top. In image 1 the conveyor and furniture tops are 56 pixels above the ground. Do NOT convert square tops into diamonds or squashed rectangles and do NOT force a diagonally receding third side face onto aligned furniture. The end-on side face can collapse. Use shading and the front face for volume as in image 2.
Mathematically the intended environment is screenX=anchorX+cell*x, screenY=anchorY+cell*depth-cell*height, depth toward viewer and height upward. This is camera/art direction, not text to print. Treat this environment as its own layer.

CHARACTER PROJECTION:
Characters use a DIFFERENT ordinary orthographic art view around 35 degrees elevation, square pixels and NO vertical projection stretch. Preserve image 3's pleasing naturally proportioned compact blocky heads, short bodies, arms and legs. Their low-poly faces must stay cute and undistorted. Do not apply the environment's sqrt(2) vertical stretch to people and do not warp the entire finished picture.
Register each person at the environment's indicated ground root or raised seat contact point, with consistent character size everywhere. Two white-uniformed chefs with tall faceted white hats stand at the two cyan crosses beside the prep stands and belt. Two walking customers at the left cyan crosses: orange cap/green backpack and brunette/pink shirt. Four diners sit on the BACKLESS stools at the orange contact dots: green-shirt brunette and pink-haired yellow-shirt diner to the right, blue-shirt glasses customer and green-cap customer below the horizontal belt. Hips must touch the seat top, feet and legs must hang/stand convincingly, and hands/chopsticks meet food on the adjacent dining ledges. Feet on floor and bodies on stools, no floating.

FINISHED ART:
Red-rimmed charcoal L-shaped conveyor with geometric salmon nigiri, tamago and maki on small cream plates. Four small wooden dining ledges and simple backless wooden stools, two prep stands, sparse clear gameplay aisle. Keep the guide's L arrangement and square footprints; square stools/serving tables really show square tops rather than short perspective trapezoids. A wooden sushi entrance with red fish-symbol noren and glowing yellow lanterns at the top, angular potted green plants, faceted slate rocks, crates, little orange cones and yellow/black expansion boundaries along the outside grey border areas of the guide.
Clean broad matte flat-shaded polygonal planes, minimal texture, crisp low-poly silhouettes, soft grounded ambient occlusion, warm inviting gold light, cream/red/honey wood/green palette. The surroundings look like the restaurant reference rendered with the underwater example's environment view. Uniform lighting across the two art projections.
Fill the guide's blank top-left UI panel with a faceted gold coin and exact text "1,240". Fill its three blank cream buttons with hammer, chef head, and green-cushioned BACKLESS stool icons, respectively, with crisp dark outlines only on the UI. One small white sushi order bubble, one heart and a little music note may reinforce cheerful restaurant life as in image 3.
One finished full-bleed opaque portrait 2:3 gameplay concept, 1024x1536, not a guide or diagram. Remove all cyan crosses, orange contact dots, and placeholder marks. No annotations, equations, extra text, title, watermark or device frame.
Avoid the previous restaurant's conventional perspective floor, receding rows, flattened top faces, tall stretched characters, isometric diamonds, chair backrests, painterly textures, outlines around scene objects, clutter in the aisle, and any underwater animals, mines, submarines, blue-ocean scenery or ocean HUD.

historical_seed_generation.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: restaurant management game theme concept art, one polished portrait gameplay screen, 2:3 aspect ratio, high resolution.

INPUT ROLES:
Image 1 (doodle-lowpoly.png) is the PRIMARY STYLE AND UI REFERENCE. Use its chunky low-poly 3D art, simple cheerful block-built chibi characters, modular wooden furniture, geometric sushi, warm lantern light, cream HUD surfaces, and simple legible icons.
Image 2 (01-doodle.png) is the RESTAURANT COMPOSITION AND GAMEPLAY REFERENCE: use the restaurant on its LEFT HALF only. Expand that restaurant into a complete standalone portrait game screen. Its right-hand underwater scene is outside this request.
Image 3 (lowpoly_character.png) reinforces the intended low-poly character design, faceted materials, warm lighting, and bright friendly palette.

PRIMARY REQUEST:
Create a cohesive, beautiful, playable-looking concept screenshot of a cozy sushi conveyor restaurant undergoing expansion, in the low-poly style of the catalog. Show a central one-cell-wide L-shaped conveyor with a long vertical run and a rightward horizontal foot, red rim and charcoal moving surface, carrying a few clearly readable salmon nigiri, tamago, and maki on small cream plates. Two white-uniformed chefs in tall angular chef hats work on its left beside small preparation stands. Four friendly customers dine on SINGLE-CELL BACKLESS WOODEN STOOLS along the right side and lower side of the belt, with hands/chopsticks meeting the food naturally; two other customers walk in the open left aisle. Use the catalog's simple blocky hair, rectangular limbs, expressive tiny faces, and appealing compact proportions. Keep the belt geometry and characters easy to read at phone size.

ENVIRONMENT AND THEME:
Warm pale sandstone square-tile floor with restrained visible seams; a wood sushi entrance with red fish-symbol noren at the top, a glowing yellow lantern, and potted angular green plants. The room has a warm golden interior and compact unfinished expansion pockets at the outer edges: faceted slate rocks, wooden crates, small construction cones and narrow yellow/black boundary strips, as in the restaurant reference. Rich red conveyor trim, honey-brown wood, cream, charcoal and emerald green, with little pink/coral clothing accents. Cozy evening harbor-shop character comes through warm wooden beams and lanterns; keep the floor and gameplay bright and uncluttered. Broad matte polygonal planes, clean flat shading, gentle ambient occlusion, soft warm grounded shadows, no painted texture.

CRITICAL ENVIRONMENT PROJECTION: square top/front oblique projection.
This is a custom parallel-projection, layered 2.5D game composition. Logical coordinates are (x, depth, height), positive depth toward the viewer, positive height upward. Use screenX = anchorX + cell*x; screenY = anchorY + cell*depth - cell*height. Treat this as a rendering instruction, never print equations in the art.
Every ground tile is a TRUE SCREEN-ALIGNED SQUARE, same width and height throughout the image. Tile seams form straight horizontal and straight vertical lines with perfectly uniform pitch in both directions, all the way from the entrance to the bottom. No rotation of the square grid into diamonds, no camera yaw, no vanishing-point convergence, no distant tile shrinkage, and no compressed rectangular floor cells.
Grid-aligned TOP planes and FRONT planes are true-shape; a unit top and a unit front each display as a square, rather than a slanted parallelogram. A square tabletop or square conveyor module has screen-horizontal and screen-vertical top edges. Height rises straight upward above each footprint, overlapping the row behind; an object's footprint remains registered on its ground cell. The end-on side plane can collapse; do not force the usual isometric third visible face. Furniture and architecture obey this projection consistently.
Characters and rounded dishes may use a separate ordinary orthographic art view around 35 degrees elevation for pleasing undistorted proportions, registered at the same logical ground root and cell scale as the terrain. Do not vertically stretch finished character art. Match all sitting/standing attachment points explicitly: feet on floor, hips on stool seats, hands near plates.

SCREEN COMPOSITION AND UI:
Portrait 2:3, restaurant gameplay occupies nearly the full screen. Give the square grid and open aisle enough space to be obvious. Top-left: one compact cream rounded coin counter with a faceted gold coin and EXACT text "1,240". Bottom-left: three consistent cream rounded-square buttons with dark brown rim and subtle depth, containing a hammer, chef head, and green stool icon respectively, as in the restaurant reference. No text labels on these buttons. Tiny white salmon-order bubble over one walking customer and one small heart near a happy diner. Keep the central play space free of large overlays.
Render a single integrated game scene, not a component catalog, tiled contact sheet, split view, phone/device mockup, poster, or titled presentation board. No additional HUD features, extra text, watermarks, or logos.

STYLE AVOID:
Hand-drawn linework around the scene, painterly airbrush, paper grain, realistic surface textures, intricate tiny decoration, smooth clay sculpture, pixel art, diamond-grid isometric projection, conventional perspective camera, diagonally receding floor lines, stretched character heads, and busy clutter inside the playable aisle.
